source.title: TONINO PICULA - O Srbiji nakon izbora ,tko stoji iza studenata PODCAST ČUŠPAJZ#167

summary.title_hr: Tonino Picula – O Srbiji nakon izbora, tko stoji iza studenata (Podcast Čušpajz #167)
summary.abstract_hr: U ovoj epizodi podcasta Čušpajz voditelj razgovara s Toninom Piculom, zastupnikom u Europskom parlamentu i stalnim izvjestiteljem za Srbiju, o parlamentarnim izborima u Srbiji održanima 25. listopada, na kojima je studentska lista porazila Aleksandra Vučića s razlikom od oko pola milijuna glasova. Picula objašnjava kako je studentski pokret preko plenuma djelovao tajnovito i učinkovito te ističe da sada mora prijeći u fazu personifikacije i brzo preuzeti odgovornost vlasti, uz upozorenje da se Vučića i njegovu 'duboku državu' ne smije podcjenjivati. Razgovor se dotiče i posljedica promjene vlasti za Hrvatsku i regiju, uključujući nestale u Domovinskom ratu, BiH i Milorada Dodika, Kosovo i Crnu Goru. Govori se i o nemirima u državama EU-a, ruskoj prijetnji, politici Donalda Trumpa, stanju hrvatske politike te o umjetnoj inteligenciji. Picula zaključuje da je Europska unija unatoč problemima vrijedna borbe te da Hrvatska ne treba imati komplekse prema Srbiji.
key_topics: odnosi srbije s hrvatskom i regijom
nemiri i nezadovoljstvo građana u europskoj uniji
rusija, ukrajina i politika donalda trumpa
key_points: Picula nije bio iznenađen smjerom događaja u Srbiji, ali ističe da nitko nije mogao predvidjeti tako plebiscitarnu pobjedu studentske liste, s razlikom od oko pola milijuna glasova i nezapamćeno visokim odazivom. Prema njegovim riječima, studentima su kao generalna proba pomogli lokalni izbori održani šest mjeseci ranije.

Prema Piculi, Vučić je brzo priznao poraz jer je odustao od scenarija isprovociranih nereda. Picula očekuje da će Vučić iz oporbe, uz pomoć 'duboke države' koju je gradio 14 godina, opstruirati novu vlast i čekati njezino trošenje.

O studentskoj listi zna se malo jer su odluke donošene na plenumima s kojih gotovo ništa nije iscurilo. Picula smatra da pokret sada mora prijeći iz faze tajnovitosti u fazu personifikacije i mora brzo djelovati jer si ne može dopustiti ni uobičajenih 100 dana.

Izbori su prema Piculi doveli do potpunog reseta srbijanske političke scene: dosadašnja oporba je praktički nestala, a Socijalistička partija Srbije prvi put od 1990. nije ušla u parlament. Očekuje da ni studentska lista ni Vučićeva stranka neće zadržati sadašnji oblik u idućih pola godine.

Za odnose s Hrvatskom Picula smatra ključnim da nova vlast u Srbiji, uz verbalnu distancu od devedesetih, i politikom pokaže odgovornost. To uključuje otvaranje arhiva u Beogradu radi rasvjetljavanja sudbine nestalih u Domovinskom ratu.

Nemire u državama EU-a Picula pripisuje nagomilanoj frustraciji građana zbog stanovanja, slabljenja srednjeg sloja, školstva i mirovina. Navodi tri megatrenda: više sukoba uz slabljenje multilateralizma, fragmentaciju političke scene i ubrzanje svega. Unatoč tome smatra da je EU jedan od prostora u kojima se najbolje živi i da se za nju vrijedi boriti.

Picula smatra da Hrvatska ne smije imati komplekse i da se ne treba bojati brzog ulaska Srbije u EU. Srbija će se, prema njegovoj procjeni, još dugo baviti sama sobom, odnosno vladavinom prava, korupcijom, mafijom i slobodom tiska.
key_topics_en: student movement and the student list
serbia's relations with croatia and the region
european integration of the western balkans
unrest and citizen dissatisfaction in the european union
russia, ukraine, and the policy of donald trump
key_points_en: Picula was not surprised by the direction of events in Serbia, but emphasizes that no one could have predicted such a plebiscitary victory for the student list, with a margin of about half a million votes and an unprecedentedly high turnout. According to his words, the local elections held six months earlier served the students as a dress rehearsal.

According to Picula, Vučić quickly conceded defeat because he abandoned the scenario of provoked unrest. Picula expects that Vučić from the opposition, with the help of the 'deep state' he built for 14 years, will obstruct the new government and wait for its wearing down.

Little is known about the student list because decisions were made at plenums from which almost nothing leaked. Picula believes that the movement must now transition from the phase of secrecy to the phase of personification and must act quickly because it cannot afford even the usual 100 days.

According to Picula, the elections led to a complete reset of the Serbian political scene: the previous opposition has practically disappeared, and the Socialist Party of Serbia did not enter parliament for the first time since 1990. He expects that neither the student list nor Vučić's party will maintain their current form in the next six months.

For relations with Croatia, Picula considers it crucial that the new government in Serbia, along with a verbal distance from the nineties, also show responsibility through policy. This includes opening the archives in Belgrade in order to shed light on the fate of those missing in the Homeland War.

Picula attributes the unrest in EU countries to accumulated citizen frustration over housing, the weakening of the middle class, schooling, and pensions. He cites three megatrends: more conflicts accompanied by the weakening of multilateralism, fragmentation of the political scene, and the acceleration of everything. Despite this, he believes that the EU is one of the spaces where people live best and that it is worth fighting for.

Picula believes that Croatia must not have complexes and that it should not fear Serbia's quick entry into the EU. Serbia, according to his assessment, will for a long time deal with itself, namely with the rule of law, corruption, the mafia, and freedom of the press.
summary.title_en: Tonino Picula – On Serbia After the Elections, Who Stands Behind the Students (Podcast Čušpajz #167)
summary.abstract_en: In this episode of the podcast Čušpajz, the host speaks with Tonino Picula, Member of the European Parliament and permanent rapporteur for Serbia, about the parliamentary elections in Serbia held on October 25, in which the student list defeated Aleksandar Vučić with a margin of about half a million votes. Picula explains how the student movement acted secretly and effectively through plenums and emphasizes that it must now transition into the phase of personification and quickly assume the responsibility of governing, with a warning that Vučić and his 'deep state' must not be underestimated. The conversation also touches upon the consequences of the change of government for Croatia and the region, including those missing in the Homeland War, BiH and Milorad Dodik, Kosovo, and Montenegro. They also discuss unrest in EU countries, the Russian threat, the policy of Donald Trump, the state of Croatian politics, and artificial intelligence. Picula concludes that despite its problems, the European Union is worth fighting for and that Croatia should not have complexes regarding Serbia.
